2021_15_bylaws_of_the_oakland_county_sch.paragraph: Bylaws of the Oakland County School Boards Association, circulated with proposed 2021 amendments printed in red, govern the Association's offices, membership, dues, meetings, election of directors, officers, committees, fiduciary duties, indemnification and amendment procedure. The text records adoption by the Board of Directors on 11/15/2017, adoption by the General Membership on 1/24/2018 and 10/18/2018, and amendments adopted by the General Membership on 9/16/2020. The most consequential proposed change is a new Article VI, Section 1 fixing the Board of Directors at an odd number of no fewer than 7 nor more than 9 Directors, with the Board given discretion to set the number and to shrink it by attrition.
2021_15_bylaws_of_the_oakland_county_sch.page:
**Identification**
Bylaws of the Oakland County School Boards Association (the "Association"), a Michigan nonprofit. Adopted by Board of Directors 11/15/2017; adopted by General Membership 1/24/2018 and 10/18/2018; amendments adopted by General Membership 9/16/2020. Proposed 2021 amendments appear in red within the text.

**Articles I-II: Offices and Purpose**
Principal office at 2111 Pontiac Lake Road, Waterford Township, County of Oakland. A registered office and registered agent are continuously maintained. Stated purposes include advancing public education quality in Oakland County through cooperative effort of locally elected boards, conducting meetings and programs in partnership with Oakland Schools, and advocating for county, state and national legislation supporting public education.

**Articles III-V: Membership, Dues, Member Meetings**
Members are publicly elected board members of Oakland County school districts or the Oakland ISD Board of Education whose district is in good standing with the Michigan Association of School Boards (MASB). One vote per Member, in person; exceptions give each Member School District one (1) vote on committee-chair selection, resolutions (Article IX) and bylaws amendments (Article XVI). Electronic voting is reserved to the Board of Directors for emergency business, reaffirmed at the next Board meeting. Membership is not transferable. Financing comes from an annual MASB grant to County Area School Boards Association (CASBA) members, ISD dues not exceeding that grant, plus contributions and gifts. An annual meeting plus not less than three additional regular membership meetings are held yearly; the annual meeting is the first regular meeting after July 1. Special meetings require 30 days' notice; written notice of meetings is delivered not less than ten nor more than fifty days ahead. Quorum is at least one Member from twenty-five (25%) percent of Member School Districts.

**Articles VI-VIII: Directors and Officers**
Proposed new Section 1 sets an odd number of Directors, no fewer than 7 nor more than 9; decreases occur by attrition (possibly an eight-member Board for up to one year), increases by election. Terms are three (3) years. By May 1 the Board convenes an Election Committee of the three most recently elected Directors; elections occur at the June meeting; no floor nominations. Failure to attend three (3) consecutive Board meetings constitutes resignation unless excused on written request within thirty (30) days. Officers are President, Vice-President, Secretary and Treasurer, elected from the Board; Directors and officers receive no stated salaries. Board records and proceedings are confidential absent advance authorization.

**Articles IX-XVI: Committees, Finances, Indemnification**
Committee quorum is twenty-five (25%) percent of appointed representatives; chairs are elected annually at the first meeting after January 31 with seven (7) calendar days' written notice. The Government Relations Committee meets at least 6 times per year and submits Legislative Priorities to the Board by June 15. The Resolutions and Bylaws Committee meets at least once per year; Member School District voting windows run at least forty (40) calendar days; resolutions approved by at least nineteen (19) Member School Districts become official Association positions. Expenditures over $2,500 require Board approval plus President and Treasurer signatures; up to $2,500 either officer may approve. The Treasurer presents an annual budget (July 1 to June 30) by June 30 and an actual income and expense report by August 30. Article XII provides indemnification under the Michigan Nonprofit Association Act. Article XVI amendments require a written ballot to each Member School District with at least a forty (40) day voting period.

**Appendix 1**
"Definition of Cause for Removing a Board Member or Officer," adopted by the OCSBA Board of Directors September 16, 2020, framed around the duties of care, loyalty and obedience.
2021_15_bylaws_of_the_oakland_county_sch.verbose:
**Identity and adoption history**
"Bylaws of the Oakland County School Boards Association" with proposed 2021 amendments printed in red. Header records: Adopted by Board of Directors 11/15/2017; Adopted by General Membership 1/24/2018 and 10/18/2018; Amendments Adopted by General Membership 9/16/2020. Articles I through XVI plus Appendix 1.

**Articles I-II: Offices and Purpose**
The principal office is at 2111 Pontiac Lake Road, Waterford Township, County of Oakland; other offices within or without Michigan may be established by the Board of Directors, and a registered office and registered agent are continuously maintained. Purposes (a) through (h): advance the quality of public education in Oakland County through cooperative efforts of locally elected boards of education; promote high standards in educational programs and services for all students; inform school board members on educational issues; sponsor meetings and programs in partnership with Oakland Schools; promote public understanding of the role of school boards; enhance cooperation among Oakland County boards; represent Oakland County school board views to political representatives; and advocate for legislation supporting public education services by locally elected boards.

**Article III - Membership**
Eligible Members are publicly elected Board of Education members of school districts located in Oakland County, or elected Oakland ISD Board of Education members ("Member School Districts"), whose district is a member in good standing of the Michigan Association of School Boards ("MASB"). Each Member has one vote, cast in person. Exception: each Member School District has one (1) vote on selecting a committee chair, on resolutions (Article IX) and on amending the Bylaws (Article XVI); district votes are recorded on receipt of the completed resolution or ballot indicating the vote of the district's Trustees, must arrive before the stated deadline, and results go to all Member Districts no later than the next general membership meeting. Electronic voting is granted to the Board of Directors only for emergency business, reaffirmed at the next Board meeting. Membership is not transferable or assignable.

**Articles IV-V - Dues and Member Meetings**
Financing comes from an annual MASB grant to its County Area School Boards Association (CASBA) members, Intermediate School District membership dues not exceeding the MASB CASBA grant, and contributions and gifts. An annual meeting plus not less than three additional regular membership meetings are held each year; the annual meeting is the first regular meeting after July 1. Special meetings may be called by voice or email by the President or by two or more Directors with 30 days' notice, and written notice is delivered personally or by email by the Secretary not less than ten nor more than fifty days before a meeting. Quorum is at least one Member from twenty-five (25%) percent of the Member School Districts.

**Article VI - Election of Board of Directors (renumbered by the 2021 amendments)**
New Section 1, Number of Directors: an odd number, no fewer than 7 nor more than 9; the Board has discretion over the number and shall consider a change whenever an election produces fewer candidates than open seats and before seeking candidates to fill a vacancy under Section 6; the Secretary promptly communicates any change to all Members; decreases occur by attrition, which may result in an eight member Board for up to one year until the next election, and increases by election. Eligibility: only one Member from each Member School District may serve at a time. Term: three (3) years, continuing until a successor is elected and qualified. Board Election: by May 1 yearly the Board convenes an Election Committee of the three most recently elected Directors, which seeks candidates providing geographical balance throughout Oakland County; Board Candidate Application Forms go to all Member School Districts; nominations cannot be made from the floor; election takes place at the June meeting; more candidates than vacancies means a written ballot, fewer means the Board fills the vacancy at its next meeting. Resignation/Removal: removal by the Members or the Board, with cause as defined in Appendix I, by majority affirmative vote excluding the Director subject to the action. Vacancy: the Board first considers decreasing the number of Directors under Section 1; if the number is retained, the President notifies the Members, each district receives a Board Candidate Application Form, and the Board appoints for the remainder of the vacated term until the next scheduled election. Attendance: failure to attend three (3) consecutive Board meetings constitutes a resignation, though a Director may be granted an excused absence on written request to the Board President within thirty (30) days of the missed meeting.

**Articles VII-VIII - Board and Officers**
The Board carries out the purposes specified in Article II of the Articles of Incorporation. Special meetings may be called by the President or any two Directors, with at least two days' notice personally, by phone, fax or email, or five days' notice by mail. Quorum is a majority of the Board, and Directors receive no stated salaries. Action without a meeting requires written consent signed by all Directors, and Board proceedings are confidential absent advance authorization. Officers, elected from the current Board, are a President, Vice-President, Secretary and Treasurer, serving until the next annual meeting and removable with cause by majority vote. The President is Chief Executive Officer; the Secretary records all votes and minutes; the Treasurer holds custody of funds and securities and may be required to furnish a bond at the Association's cost.

**Article IX - Committees**
Committee quorum is twenty-five (25%) percent of appointed representatives, each present representative having one vote; alternates count for quorum or vote only when the primary representative is absent. Each standing and ad hoc committee elects a Chairperson annually as the first order of business at its first meeting after January 31, with written notice at least seven (7) calendar days prior; chairs set schedules and agendas, maintain attendance records, distribute minutes and report to the Board through the President, and may be removed without cause. The Government Relations Committee is a standing committee meeting at least 6 times per year, with a representative appointed by each Member School District at its annual organizational meeting, one (1) vote per district in attendance, and Legislative Priorities submitted to the Board for approval by June 15. The Resolutions and Bylaws Committee is a standing committee meeting at least once per year; revisions may be initiated by a Member School District Board, the Board of Directors, the Government Relations Committee or the Resolutions and Bylaws Committee; the district voting window is at least forty (40) calendar days; and resolutions approved by at least nineteen (19) Member School Districts become the official position of the Association.

**Articles X-XVI**
On dissolution, assets are distributed as provided in Article VIII of the Articles of Incorporation, with no inurement to any Member, Director or Officer as prohibited by Section 501(c)(4) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 as amended, the Michigan General Sales Tax Act or the Michigan Use Tax Act. Article XI: expenditures may not exceed the approved annual budget; Board approval plus signature by both the President and Treasurer are required for any expenditure exceeding $2,500, while expenditures up to $2,500 require approval by either the President or the Treasurer, and the Vice-President may approve if both are absent or disabled. Financial reports go to Board members quarterly or on request; the Treasurer presents an annual budget (July 1 to June 30) by June 30 and an annual actual income and expense report by August 30, both presented at the first fall Member Meeting. Agreed-upon procedures are performed annually; an external audit replaces them only if required by law or a third party. The Board may enter an Administrative and Financial Services Agreement with Oakland Schools, monitored by the Treasurer. Article XII indemnifies directors and officers to the fullest extent authorized by the Michigan Nonprofit Association Act ("the Act"), with indemnification approved by a disinterested quorum vote, a committee of not less than two (2) disinterested Directors, or independent legal counsel in a written opinion. Article XIII leaves the fiscal year to the Board. Article XIV requires avoidance of conflicts, and a conflicted Director is not counted toward quorum. Article XV covers contracts and borrowing by Board resolution, action by written consent, Section 7 Remote Participation in Meeting by Telephone (two-way communication constituting presence in person), and a corporate seal inscribed with the Association name, "Corporate Seal" and "Michigan". Article XVI, retitled "AMENDMENTS, RULES AND REGULATIONS," provides for amendment by vote of the Member School Districts on a written ballot with at least a forty (40) day voting period and one vote per district, and permits the Board to set aside rules during a declared local, state or national emergency.

**Appendix 1 - Definition of Cause for Removing a Board Member or Officer**
Adopted by the OCSBA Board of Directors September 16, 2020. The preface sets out three primary legal duties: duty of care (prudent use of all assets, including facility, people and good will), duty of loyalty (advancing the mission, disclosing conflicts of interest, deciding in the nonprofit's best interest), and duty of obedience (obeying applicable laws and regulations, following its own bylaws, adhering to stated corporate purposes). Cause includes willful failure to follow OCSBA bylaws; willful neglect of duties; failure to disclose a conflict of interest or using the Association for personal gain; using the OCSBA Board position or OCSBA's logo in a political endorsement; frequently missed Board or committee meetings; creating an unhealthy or dysfunctional boardroom through inappropriate behavior or disrespect; ethical concerns such as discrimination, harassment or criminal behaviors; and acts of malfeasance, misfeasance or nonfeasance. Removal should be done only when absolutely necessary, with the reasons left to the Association's other Directors and Members.

2021_17_resolutions_proposed_2021.paragraph: Oakland County School Boards Association's 2021 Proposed Resolutions and Amendments packet, marking deletions and additions, puts new items before Member School Districts and reprints the continuing resolutions adopted by OCSBA's Member School Districts on September 14, 2019. The 2021 items are a proposed amendment to the School Finance Research Collaborative resolution originally adopted 9/24/2019, a proposed Broadband Access and Devices resolution tied to MASB Resolution A-10.30, and a Teacher Shortages resolution drawn from the MASB 2021-2022 Legislative Priority.
2021_17_resolutions_proposed_2021.page:
**Format**
"2021 Proposed Resolutions & Amendments," with a key indicating struck text as Deletion and capitalized text as ADDITION. Each item pairs a Legislative Priority with a proposed resolution or amendment, a bracketed cross-reference to the corresponding Michigan Association of School Boards (MASB) resolution, and a rationale.

**School Finance Research Collaborative (SFRC) - proposed amendment**
Legislative Priority (Rev. 2021): review and implement SFRC recommendations, including the recommended additional studies on capital costs, infrastructure and transportation, while holding higher funded districts harmless. The proposed amendment, to the original resolution adopted 9/24/2019, restates OCSBA support and adds in capitals that WHILE IMPLEMENTING THE SFRC RECOMMENDATIONS, HIGHER FUNDED DISTRICTS MUST BE HELD HARMLESS. Cross-referenced to MASB resolution G 11.01 and A-10.25 - 2021 amendment. Rationale: continued support for raising all districts to SFRC funding levels toward equitable funding, opposition to legislation lowering any district's current funding, and alignment with a MASB proposed 2021 amendment.

**Broadband Access and Devices - proposed resolution**
Legislative Priority: expand access to quality internet and proper devices for all students and staff. Proposed resolution: broadband should be included in any federal or state infrastructure plan; support for additional federal and state funding to expand affordable and reliable broadband access; support for federal and state programs for the purchase of internet capable devices and software. Cross-referenced to MASB Resolution A-10.30 - 2021 amendment. Rationale cites pandemic-highlighted inequities in access to reliable broadband and devices.

**Teacher Shortages - proposed resolution**
Legislative Priority: implement state-based programs to address teacher shortages and retain teachers. Proposed resolution supports statewide initiatives while maintaining quality teacher preparation programs, listing possible incentives to enter and complete a teaching college program, incentives for teachers to remain in the classroom, and easing the process to obtain Michigan certification for teachers certified in other states. Cross-referenced to the MASB 2021-2022 Legislative Priority.

**Continuing resolutions adopted September 14, 2019**

| Resolution | MASB / NSBA reference |
|---|---|
| Mental Health | G 9.01; G 9.05; G 9.50 |
| Local Control | A 10.10; A 10.55; A 12.70 |
| Evidence-Based Decision Making | G 11.01 |
| Unfunded Mandates | A 10.20 |
| School Finance Research Collaborative | G 11.01 (2021 amendment proposed) |
| School Aid A-E | A 10.25 and subparts; A 10.05; A 10.55 |
| Accountability and Transparency | A 6.65 (c), (d), (f) |
| Universal Preschool | A 6.15 (c) |
| Special Education / IDEA | A 5.01; NSBA Advocacy: IDEA |

The School Aid resolution has five parts: oppose using School Aid Fund dollars for any purpose other than K-12 education; support additional funding for Special Education, At-Risk and ELL students; protect the School Aid Fund and local revenues from state tax policy changes; specify in Michigan's Constitution that the School Aid Fund is only for Pre-K to 12th grade public education and oppose private school voucher or tax credit programs; and enact the annual School Aid Budget no later than June 1 so districts can meet the June 30 budget deadline. A Lame Duck resolution addresses accelerated passage of legislation after the November election. When aligned with its own priorities OCSBA also supports the NSBA, MASB and Oakland County Superintendents Association (OCSA) legislative agendas. Links given: https://www.masb.org/resolutions.aspx and https://www.nsba.org/Advocacy.
2021_17_resolutions_proposed_2021.verbose:
**Packet identity and conventions**
"2021 PROPOSED RESOLUTIONS & AMENDMENTS" of the Oakland County School Boards Association (OCSBA), with a key for amendments showing struck text as Deletion and capitalized text as ADDITION. The packet is organized as Legislative Priority statements followed by the proposed resolution or amendment text, a bracketed cross-reference to Michigan Association of School Boards (MASB) resolution numbers, and a rationale; the continuing resolutions previously adopted by Member School Districts are reprinted at the end.

**School Finance Research Collaborative (SFRC) - proposed amendment**
Legislative Priority (Rev. 2021), printed in the source with the heading typo "SCHOL FINANCE RESEARCH COLLABORATIVE": review and implement recommendations of the SFRC including the recommended additional studies on capital costs, infrastructure, and transportation; while implementing the SFRC recommendations, higher funded districts must be held harmless. The proposed amendment notes the original resolution was adopted 9/24/2019 and reads: "SCHOOL FINANCE RESEARCH COLLABORATIVE (SFRC): OCSBA supports review and implementation of the recommendations of the SFRC, including the recommended additional studies on capital costs, infrastructure, and transportation. WHILE IMPLEMENTING THE SFRC RECOMMENDATIONS, HIGHER FUNDED DISTRICTS MUST BE HELD HARMLESS." Cross-reference: MASB resolution G 11.01 and A-10.25 - 2021 amendment. Rationale: "We continue to support increasing all districts to the funding levels recommended by the SFRC, with a goal of achieving equitable funding for all districts. We oppose legislation that would lower any district's current funding in the process. This proposed amendment is aligned with a MASB proposed 2021 amendment." For a comparatively high-revenue district such as Troy, the hold-harmless addition is the operative clause.

**Broadband Access and Devices - proposed resolution**
Legislative Priority: expand access to quality internet and proper devices for all students and staff. Proposed resolution text: broadband should be included in any federal or state infrastructure plan; OCSBA supports additional federal and state funding opportunities to expand affordable and reliable broadband access; and supports federal and state programs for the purchase of internet capable devices and software. Cross-reference: MASB Resolution A-10.30 - 2021 amendment. Rationale: broadband is an important component of school infrastructure, the pandemic highlighted inequities in access to reliable broadband and devices, and the amendment is aligned with a proposed 2021 MASB Amendment.

**Teacher Shortages - proposed resolution**
Legislative Priority: implement state-based programs to address teacher shortages and to retain teachers. Proposed resolution: OCSBA supports statewide initiatives to address teacher shortages and retain teachers while maintaining quality teacher preparation programs; initiatives might include, but should not be limited to, incentives to enter and complete a teaching college program, incentives for teachers to remain in the classroom, and easing the process to obtain Michigan certification for teachers that are certified in other states. Cross-reference: MASB 2021-2022 Legislative Priority.

**Continuing resolutions adopted by OCSBA's Member School Districts on September 14, 2019**
MENTAL HEALTH: OCSBA supports increased mental health services and professionals in schools and providing adequate state resources to allow schools both to educate and to keep students and staff safe [MASB Resolutions G 9.01; G 9.05; G 9.50]. Two sub-points: help staff identify potential mental health issues for students; and encourage the Michigan Department of Education (MDE) to develop a model policy for staff regarding identifying mental health issues and appropriate staff response.
LOCAL CONTROL: support local control of community-governed public schools with elected school boards [MASB Resolution A 10.10; A 10.55; A 12.70].
EVIDENCE-BASED DECISION MAKING: OCSBA supports evidence-based education policy that will maximize opportunities for the highest achievement of each student [MASB Resolution G 11.01].
UNFUNDED MANDATES: OCSBA opposes any state or federal legislation that results in increased costs for school districts without full funding, and encourages the Michigan Legislature to oppose any federal laws or programs that are not fully funded and thus cost the state valuable resources [MASB Resolution A 10.20].
SCHOOL FINANCE RESEARCH COLLABORATIVE (SFRC): the continuing form of the resolution, supporting review and implementation of SFRC recommendations including additional studies on capital costs, infrastructure and transportation [MASB Resolution G 11.01], flagged "* 2021 - AMENDMENT PROPOSED *".

**School Aid resolution, parts A through E**
A. Oppose using School Aid Fund dollars for any other purpose than K-12 education [MASB Resolution A 10.25]. B. Support additional funding for Special Education, At-Risk and ELL students [MASB Resolutions A 10.25 (g) and (j); A 10.55]. C. Protect the School Aid Fund and local revenues from state tax policy changes [MASB Resolutions A 10.25 (c); A 10.55]. D. Specify that the School Aid Fund is only for Pre-K to 12th grade public education in Michigan's Constitution and oppose any attempts to create private school voucher or tax credit programs [MASB Resolutions A 10.25 (a) and A 10.05]. E. OCSBA supports enacting the annual School Aid Budget no later than June 1 so that school districts have factual information to meet their constitutional/statutory requirement to approve a budget by June 30 [MASB Resolution A 10.25 (h)].

**Remaining continuing resolutions**
ACCOUNTABILITY AND TRANSPARENCY: OCSBA supports transparency and accountability for ALL school aid funds, naming community governed public school districts, charter schools, cyber schools, community colleges and public universities [MASB Resolution A 6.65 (c), (d), (f)].
LAME DUCK: OCSBA supports lame duck parameters that will address introduction and accelerated passage of legislation after the November election.
UNIVERSAL PRESCHOOL: OCSBA supports additional new dollars to fund universal preschool for all four year old children [MASB Resolution A 6.15 (c)].
SPECIAL EDUCATION: OCSBA supports full funding of the federal Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA), noting that although federal legislation initially promised to provide 40 percent of the excess cost to educate students with disabilities, appropriations have fallen short, leaving states and local school districts to make up the difference [MASB Resolution A 5.01; NSBA Advocacy: IDEA].

**Aligned external agendas and references**
When aligned with OCSBA Legislative Priorities, OCSBA also supports the National School Boards Association (NSBA) Legislative Agenda, the Michigan Association of School Boards (MASB) Legislative Agenda, and the Oakland County Superintendents Association (OCSA) Legislative Agenda. Links provided: MASB Resolutions at https://www.masb.org/resolutions.aspx and NSBA Advocacy: IDEA at https://www.nsba.org/Advocacy. The packet is the ballot material a member board such as Troy School District's Board of Education would act on before these proposals can become official positions of the Association.

2021_18_summary_of_2021_proposed_bylaws_.paragraph: Three-page tabular crosswalk titled "Summary of 2021 Proposed Bylaws Amendments" for the Oakland County School Boards Association, listing for each change the page, article, section, the proposed language with current text in black and additions or deletions in red, and a rationale. Rows cover Articles III, VI, IX, XV and XVI. The central change adds a new Article VI, Section 1 setting the Board of Directors at an odd number between 7 and 9, noting that the current bylaws do not specify a number and that the Board currently has 9 Directors serving a 29 District, 201 Member Association.
2021_18_summary_of_2021_proposed_bylaws_.page:
**Format**
"SUMMARY OF 2021 PROPOSED BYLAWS AMENDMENTS," paginated 1 of 3 through 3 of 3, in a table with columns for Page, Article, Section, Proposed Change (current language in black, added language and/or deletion in red) and Rationale.

**Article III, Membership, Section 2, Voting Rights - Exceptions (page 2)**
The exception giving each Member School District one (1) vote on selecting a committee chair, on resolutions (Article IX) and on bylaws amendments (Article XVI) is edited to strike the committee-chair clause. Rationale: move committee chair language to Article IX Committees, Election of Committee Chairs.

**Article VI, new Section 1, Number of Directors (pages 3-5)**
Adds an odd number of Directors, no fewer than 7 nor more than 9, with Board discretion over the number, reconsideration whenever an election produces fewer candidates than open seats, Secretary notice of any change, decreases by attrition that may leave an eight member Board for up to one year, and increases by election. Subsequent sections are renumbered. Rationale: the current bylaws do not specify the number of Directors (currently 9 Directors for the 29 District / 201 Member Association) and provide no process to alter it; the new language gives flexibility given multiple openings and/or a lack of candidates.

**Article VI, Section 3 to 4, Board Election (page 4)**
Retains the May 1 Election Committee of the three most recently elected Directors, geographical balance across Oakland County, Board Candidate Application Forms, no floor nominations, and election at the June meeting. The closing sentence changes to following the vacancy procedure in Section 6. Rationale: align language with Section 1.

**Article VI, Section 4 to 5, Resignation/Removal (page 4)**
Removal with cause "as defined in Appendix 1." Rationale: renumber and add reference to Appendix 1.

**Article VI, Section 5 to 6, Vacancy (page 4)**
On a vacancy the Board first considers decreasing the number of Directors under Section 1; otherwise the President notifies Members, districts receive a Board Candidate Application Form, and the Board appoints for the remainder of the vacated term. Rationale: board seats have become increasingly difficult to fill; the language allows the BOD to decrease to a 7 member BOD serving 29 Districts and 201 members and removes the requirement to fill the seat; an appointee serves up to one year, then must be elected.

**Article VI, Section 6 to 7, Attendance (page 5)**
Failure to attend three (3) consecutive Board meetings constitutes a resignation, with excused absences requested in writing within thirty (30) days. Rationale: renumber, plus a clerical correction adding "may," inadvertently omitted in 2020.

**Article IX, Committees, new Sections 2 and 3 (pages 8-9)**
Adds Quorum and Voting Rights (twenty-five (25%) percent of appointed representatives; one vote each; alternates counted only when the primary representative is absent) and Committee Chairs (annual election as first order of business at the first meeting after January 31; seven (7) calendar days' written notice; duties for schedules, agendas, attendance records, minutes and reporting to the Board through the President; removal without cause). Rationale: provide structure for any future standing or ad hoc committee; quorum and voting rights were never defined; some committees may have more than one representative per district (e.g., DEI); clarify alternates' rights; chair responsibilities and replacement were undefined.

**Article XV Section 7 and Article XVI (page 16)**
Section 7 is retitled Remote Participation in Meeting by Telephone, the rationale noting participation could be by telephone or another means of electronic communication such as Zoom or WebEx using two way audio, with video not required. The Article XVI header becomes "AMENDMENTS, RULES AND REGULATIONS" to accurately reflect the sections contained within.
2021_18_summary_of_2021_proposed_bylaws_.verbose:
**Document identity**
"SUMMARY OF 2021 PROPOSED BYLAWS AMENDMENTS," a three-page table (marked 1 of 3, 2 of 3, 3 of 3) prepared by the Oakland County School Boards Association to accompany the full marked-up bylaws. Columns: Page, Article, Section, Proposed Change with the note "[Current Language in BLACK. Added Language &/or Deletion in RED]," and Rationale. Rows address Article III, several parts of Article VI, Article IX, Article XV and Article XVI.

**Page 2, Article III Membership, Section 2 Voting Rights, Exceptions**
Proposed change: "Exceptions: Each Member School District shall have one (1) vote on any proposal to select a committee chair or vote on resolutions (as outlined in Article IX) or to amend these Bylaws (as outlined in Article XVI)." with the committee-chair language struck. Rationale: move committee chair language to Article IX Committees, Election of Committee Chairs.

**Pages 3-5, Article VI Election of Board of Directors, Section 1**
Instruction: ADD New Section 1 Language and Renumber The Subsequent Sections. New text: "Section 1: Number of Directors. The Board of Directors shall consist of an odd number of Directors, with no fewer than 7 nor more than 9 members. The Board of Directors shall have discretion to determine the number of Directors to best meet the needs of the Association. The Board shall consider such a change whenever an election produces less candidates than open seats, and prior to seeking candidates to fill a vacancy under Section 6. The Secretary shall promptly communicate any change to the number of Directors to all Members. Any decrease in the number of Directors shall be accomplished by attrition, which may result in an eight member Board for up to one year, until the next election. An increase in the number of Directors shall be accomplished by election as outlined in Section 4." Rationale: the current bylaws do not specify the number of Directors (currently 9 Directors for the 29 District / 201 Member Association), nor is there a process or provision to alter the number of Directors; the new language will give flexibility in the event of multiple openings on the Board of Directors and/or a lack of candidates for the Board of Directors.

**Page 4, Article VI, Section 3 renumbered to Section 4, Board Election**
Text: by May 1 yearly the Board shall convene an Election Committee comprised of the three most recently elected Members of the Board of Directors; the Election Committee shall seek candidates who will create a Board with a geographical balance from throughout Oakland County; Board Candidate Application Forms will also be sent to all Member School Districts to be delivered to their board members; candidates must submit a completed application to the Election Committee prior to the deadline specified on the form; nominations cannot be made from the floor during the meeting at which the election occurs; election of candidates from Member School Districts shall take place at the June meeting; if there are more candidates than vacancies the Member vote shall be by written ballot; if there are fewer candidates than vacancies the Board of Directors shall fill the vacancy at its next meeting and the appointee shall serve until the next scheduled election. The final clause is amended from "At the next election, the Election Committee will seek candidates to fill the remainder of the three year term" to directing that the procedure to fill a vacancy as outlined in Section 6 be followed. Rationale: language requires updating to align with Section 1.

**Page 4 (continued), Article VI, Section 4 renumbered to Section 5, Resignation/Removal**
Text: any Director may resign by written notice to the Association; any Director may be removed by the Members or the Board at any meeting of the Members or the Board, with cause as defined in Appendix 1, by the affirmative vote of a majority of the Members or the Directors then in office (excluding the Director who is the subject of such action). Rationale: renumber and ADD reference to Appendix 1.

**Page 4 (further), Article VI, Section 5 renumbered to Section 6, Vacancy**
Text: if a vacancy shall occur among the Board of Directors as a result of death, resignation, removal, or otherwise, the Board will first consider whether it is appropriate to decrease the number of Directors as outlined in Section 1; if the Board determines that the needs of the Association are best met by retaining the current number of Directors, the President will notify the Members of the vacancy, each Member School District shall be sent a Board Candidate Application Form, and the Board of Directors shall appoint a member to fill the vacancy at its next meeting; the appointee shall serve for the remainder of the vacated term until the next scheduled election. Rationale: Board seats have become increasingly difficult to fill; the added language allows the BOD flexibility to decrease to a 7 member BOD to serve the 29 Districts and 201 members; should the Board decide to decrease to 7 members by attrition, the new language removes the current requirement to fill the seat; an appointee will serve up to one year, then have to be elected by the Members to retain their seat.

**Page 5, Article VI, Section 6 renumbered to Section 7, Attendance**
Text: failure to attend three (3) consecutive Board meetings shall constitute a resignation; however, a Director may be granted an excused absence by action of the Board; such a request shall be made in writing to the Board President within thirty (30) days of the missed meeting. Rationale: renumber section, and a clerical correction to add "may," which was inadvertently omitted in 2020.

**Pages 8-9, Article IX Committees, Sections 2 and 3**
Instruction: ADD New Language And Renumber The Subsequent Sections. New Section 2, Quorum and Voting Rights: unless otherwise stated within the Article, the presence of twenty-five (25%) percent of the appointed representatives to a Committee will constitute a quorum and each appointed representative present in the meeting shall have one vote; Member School Districts may designate an alternate representative to any committee comprised of representatives of Member School Districts, but any appointed alternate shall only be counted for quorum and/or vote when the primary appointed representative for their District is absent. New Section 3, Committee Chairs: each standing and ad hoc committee shall elect a Chairperson annually from the appointed representatives, the election being the first order of business at the Committee's first meeting after January 31, with written notice of the election date, time and place provided to all appointed representatives not less than seven (7) calendar days prior to the meeting at which the vote will occur; each Committee Chair is responsible for establishing and distributing the meeting schedule and agendas, maintaining committee attendance records, distributing meeting minutes to the appointed representatives after each meeting, and regularly reporting to the Board of Directors through the President; any Committee Chair may resign by written notice to the Association President, and any Committee Chair may be removed by the Committee Members or the Board at any meeting of the Committee Members or the Board, without cause, by the affirmative vote of a majority of the appointed representative(s) present or the Board of Directors then in office, excluding the Committee Chair who is the subject of such action. Rationale, four bullets: this will apply to and provide structure for any future standing or ad hoc committee; quorum and voting rights were never defined for committee meetings and some committees may have more than one designated representative per Member School District (e.g., DEI); clarify voting rights for District alternates to maintain equal voting rights for all districts; and committee chair responsibilities have not been previously defined, with no current process to replace a Committee Chair.

**Page 16, Article XV Miscellaneous Provisions, Section 7**
Section 7 is retitled from "Participation in Meeting by Telephone" to "Remote Participation in Meeting by Telephone." Text: by oral or written permission of a majority of the Board of Directors, a Member of the Board of Directors or of a committee designated by the Board may participate in a meeting by means of conference telephone, or similar communications equipment by means of which all persons participating in the meeting can hear each other ("two way communication"); participation in a meeting pursuant to this Section constitutes presence in person at the meeting. Rationale: update to refer to "remote" participation, which could be by telephone or another means of electronic communication (e.g., Zoom or WebEx), using two way audio communication; video is not required.

**Page 16 (continued), Article XVI Amendments**
Section listed as N/A. The article header "ARTICLE XVI AMENDMENTS, AND ADDITIONS RULES AND REGULATIONS" is amended by striking "AND ADDITIONS" and adding "RULES AND REGULATIONS." Rationale: change the Article header to accurately reflect the sections contained within.

**Net effect**
The package is administrative rather than substantive on most points, but two changes carry practical weight for member districts: the Board of Directors may shrink from 9 to as few as 7 by attrition without being obliged to fill vacant seats, and committee governance gains a defined quorum, voting rule for alternates, and a chair election and removal process. Under the amendment procedure the summary describes, each Member School District casts one vote, which is why the packet appears on a local board agenda.

**Reading the package**
All figures are for a single month against annual budgets adopted 6/15/21, so the actual columns are not comparable in scale to the budget columns and the statements carry no variance analysis. The General Fund's approved budget is set to run expenditures above revenues for the year; the Debt Service, Food Service, Career Center, Community Service, Preschool, Facilities Rental and Capital Projects funds each report their own budget and month-to-date actual, with Troy Career Center Fund (529) the only fund budgeted and reported at exactly break-even.
